status_summary: National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (2025-02-04) directed Treasury, State, Justice, Commerce and the UN Ambassador to enforce Iran sanctions, drive Iran's oil exports to zero and complete the UN snapback, which a law-firm analysis reports took effect on 2025-09-28; Executive Order 14382 (2026-02-06) authorized tariffs on countries trading with Iran, but Executive Order 14389 (2026-02-20) ended those additional duties while keeping the national emergency in place. A US-Iran memorandum signed 2026-06-17 would have exchanged sanctions relief for a final deal, but press reports say it was declared ended on 2026-07-07 and expired in mid-August. Treasury announced Operation Economic Outcast on 2026-08-24 and on 2026-10-01 issued sectoral determinations and designations under Executive Orders 13902 and 13871 with a warning of secondary sanctions on foreign financial institutions, and Public Law 119-111 (2026-09-18) extended the Iran Sanctions Act from 2026 to 2031. Direct US-Iran talks resumed on 2026-09-22 per wire reports, and whether Iran has been denied nuclear capability is not established by the sources found.

timeline.event: NSPM-2 directs Treasury to enforce Iran sanctions and roll back relief, State and Treasury to drive Iranian oil exports to zero including those to China, Justice to pursue sanctions-evasion networks, and the UN Ambassador to work with allies to complete the UN snapback.

UN sanctions on Iran are reinstated through the snapback process, according to a DLA Piper analysis, which lists asset freezes and travel bans on 121 individuals and entities and restrictions on enrichment, missiles, arms and shipping.

Month-level date: NPR, republished by Michigan Public on 2026-08-24, reports that the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February 2026 and describes a monthslong US naval blockade that has cut off most goods to Iran; it gives no start date for the blockade.

Executive Order 14382 (91 FR 6493, document 2026-02813) authorized an additional ad valorem duty on goods from countries that acquire goods or services from Iran, subject to a Commerce finding, a State recommendation and a presidential decision; effective 2026-02-07.

Executive Order 14389 (91 FR 9437, document 2026-03832) ended the additional IEEPA duties under nine orders, including Executive Order 14382 on Iran, while stating that the underlying national emergencies remain in effect.

The US and Iran sign the Islamabad memorandum of understanding: Reuters, citing one unnamed U.S. official, reports that the President and Iran's president signed it on 2026-06-17 after a digital signing by the Vice President and Iran's chief negotiator the previous Sunday. The text read to reporters by a senior administration official and published by Axios commits the US to oil export waivers, usable frozen funds, no new sanctions pending a final deal and a phased end to the naval blockade, with sanctions ending on a schedule to be set in a final deal.
Al Jazeera reports that President Trump declared the memorandum ended and both sides suspended their commitments after clashes over Strait of Hormuz shipping in late June.
President Trump announces that the US military will restart its blockade of Iranian ports, according to the Washington Examiner.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announces Operation Economic Outcast. Axios reports about 60 entities, individuals and vessels sanctioned, several licenses suspended, expansion into digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, and a plan to give countries timelines to end Iran-related business or face secondary sanctions.

Public Law 119-111 (Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026) is enacted. Its only Iran provision, Section 201, changes the expiration year in section 13(b) of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 from 2026 to 2031.

US special envoy Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi hold about three hours of talks at the UN General Assembly, the first direct contact reported since June; Iran's stated conditions include lifting the blockade and releasing frozen assets, and President Trump says another meeting will follow.

Treasury announces further Operation Economic Outcast actions: two OFAC sectoral determinations (automotive and rail) under Executive Order 13902 and designations covering Iranian car makers, a railway company, a heavy-equipment maker and a steel and oil export network, with a warning to foreign financial institutions about secondary sanctions. The release ties the action to the US maritime blockade.

The President signs an executive order implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (Public Law 119-111): it delegates the Act's functions to State, Treasury, the Trade Representative and Energy, sets duty increases on Russian goods and on the largest importers of Russian oil and gas and evasion facilitators tied to purchases on or after 2026-10-18, and in section 4 waives those duties and most of the Act's sanctions provisions until the President or the Secretary of State determines otherwise; the order text contains no Iran-specific measure and does not mention the Iran Sanctions Act.
